headline: Stock futures point to a bounce after last week's rout, but a premarket rally is not a bottom: Washington wants answers from Nvidia, Korea fell again, and money leaving AI is showing up in India.
summary: Every close here is Friday Nov 20 (the dashboard's prices_as_of is 2026-11-20, the last session); Monday's market had not opened when this was written. Premarket, about 1:20am to 6am ET, S&P 500 futures were up about 2.1% to 2.2%, Nasdaq 100 futures about 2.9% to 3.0% and Dow futures about 1.4% to 1.6% (Investing.com; Invezz). Those are futures, not closes. On Sunday Treasury Secretary Bessent warned the Fed that overtightening could hurt the economy, and said the government wants to know who oversaw Nvidia's chip sales to China. The two year yield had its biggest drop since August 2025 on Friday, and a December hike is no longer fully priced (Investing.com). CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for about $43.9 billion in stock, and the KOSPI fell as much as about 5.8% even with a rescue fund on standby. The calm spot: India, where foreign money is flowing in and INDA broke out Friday on 1.71x volume.

regime.why: The S&P 500 is in a correction and the VIX closed at 35.89 on Nov 20, a 52 week high. A premarket bounce does not change the stance; a strong up close on rising volume, then a follow through day, would. Wednesday's PCE and GDP still decide whether the Fed hikes on Dec 9.

signals.title: Futures bounce, Bessent leans on the Fed, and Asia splits
signals.what_happened: US stock futures rose overnight after the worst week for the Nasdaq since March 2020: about 1:20am ET, S&P 500 futures were up 2.1%, Nasdaq 100 futures 2.9% and Dow futures 1.4% (Investing.com); near 6am ET Invezz had 2.24%, 3.02% and 1.58%. These are futures, not closes. On Sunday Treasury Secretary Bessent warned that overtightening by the Fed could hurt the economy, pointing to the market slide (Investing.com; Invezz; Traders and Quants). On Friday the two year yield had its biggest drop since August 2025 as traders stopped fully pricing a December hike (Investing.com). Ed Yardeni cut his year end S&P 500 target to 7,500 from 7,900 (Investing.com). In Asia, Seoul's KOSPI fell as much as about 5.8% to 4,586.80 even as the government readied its stabilization fund, unused since 2008; Taiwan rose about 2.1% on official buying and short selling limits (Korea JoongAng Daily; Invezz). Gold rebounded from a 14 month low (Investing.com).
signals.so_what: Who pays and who gets paid: a Treasury secretary pressing the Fed in public helps bonds and rate sensitive stocks if the Fed listens, and hurts the dollar's credibility if it looks political. The Fed decides on Dec 9, after Wednesday's PCE. A sharp futures bounce after a capitulation week is normal; it is the next few closes and their volume that tell you if sellers are done. Korea falling while US futures rise says the AI selling is still working through Asia's memory makers. What would make this wrong: a hot core PCE (0.4% or more for the month) that puts the hike back on the table.
signals.for_you: Swing: no entries on a premarket move. Wait for a strong up close on higher volume than the day before. Puts: premiums are rich with the VIX near 36, but none of the long term scan put candidates traded enough contracts on Nov 20 to pass (see options). Long term: nothing changes before Wednesday's PCE.

signals.title: CrowdStrike buys Zscaler for about $43.9 billion in stock
signals.what_happened: With its fiscal Q3 results Monday, CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler in an all stock deal worth about $43.9 billion. Zscaler holders get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares each, about $260.41 on the Nov 20 close, a 34% premium; both boards approved it, and Zscaler's founder and affiliates (about 34% of shares) signed support agreements (8-K; Reuters via Globe and Mail). CrowdStrike posted record net new ARR of $419 million and guided Q4 sales to $1.638 to $1.644 billion, above the $1.62 billion estimate; Zscaler's quarterly revenue rose 20% to $949.3 million (Reuters). Premarket, CrowdStrike fell about 8% to 9% and Zscaler rose 13% to 19%, depending on the report (Seeking Alpha; Benzinga). CRWD closed 229.44 and ZS 194.82 on Nov 20 (dashboard).
signals.so_what: Follow the money: the biggest security platforms are buying the rest, because whoever holds the most endpoint, network and cloud data trains the best detection. Who pays: CrowdStrike holders, through dilution, and deal traders sell CRWD to hedge their ZS buys until the deal closes. Who gets paid: ZS holders. Second order: Palo Alto now faces one rival that covers both endpoint and network, and smaller names like SentinelOne and Okta become the obvious next targets or the odd ones out. What would make this wrong: antitrust review, or CRWD falling far enough that the deal's value shrinks.
signals.for_you: Swing: no CRWD trades; it has no buy point (lower highs and lower lows), and its Nov 19 range break up already failed. Puts: no CRWD or ZS puts; deal stocks gap. Long term: CRWD is still on the TrendSpider long term scan, but the dashboard needs a higher low over 213.22 and a close over 272.29 on 1.5x volume first. ZS is under its long term zone (200.73).

signals.title: Nvidia: Bessent says Washington wants to know who oversaw its China sales
signals.since_yesterday: On CBS Sunday, Bessent said the government will look into Nvidia's chip sales to China and find out who oversaw compliance: "we do need answers." Nvidia traded up about 6% premarket Monday.
signals.what_happened: Bessent said he has been in touch with Nvidia's temporary management, lead directors and lawyers, expects a "very fulsome" answer from the board, and that the government will learn who oversaw compliance on China sales (Investing.com; Invezz). Huang and Nvidia's general counsel are due before House committees in early December; investors have proposed a class action (Investing.com). Premarket Monday, Nvidia was up about 6% (Yahoo Finance; Invezz), a premarket price, not a close. IBD reported that Arm's CEO Rene Haas took himself out of the running for Nvidia's CEO job; we could not confirm that with a second source.
signals.so_what: The question has moved from one executive's conduct to the company's export compliance, which can mean fines, new limits on China sales or restated regional numbers. That is slower to clear than a leadership change. Second order: every chip and server maker that sells into Asia through hubs is now in the same spotlight. What would make this wrong: a board report by about Nov 27 that satisfies Treasury.
signals.for_you: Swing: no chip entries this week; a premarket pop after a 23% weekly drop is a bounce until it closes up on volume. Puts: no NVDA or chip puts; the group is falling. Long term: NVDA has no buy point (under a falling 200 day at 203.09).

signals.title: Money leaving AI is landing in India: INDA broke out on 1.71x volume
signals.what_happened: Foreign investors bought more than Rs 1 lakh crore of Indian stocks in November, the first month over that mark, after selling from May to October; analysts tie it to money leaving crowded AI trades and to cheaper oil (Business Today, Nov 19; IndiaIPO). On Nov 19 the Sensex rose 990 points to 83,022 and the Nifty 286 points to 25,514 (Business Today). On Nov 20, when the S&P 500 fell 3.7%, INDA closed 52.90, over its 52.13 range top, on 10.8 million shares, 1.71 times its 50 day average (Massive). Over 3 months INDA is up 6.8% while SPY is down 9.5% (Massive, Aug 20 to Nov 20).
signals.so_what: This is the follow the money read of last week: funds that sold Korea and Taiwan chip stocks needed somewhere to go, and India is large, liquid and not an AI story. Who gets paid: Indian banks and consumer names that foreigners buy first (HDB, IBN). Risks: the RBI may hike again in December, Indian stocks trade at about 19 times forward earnings, a premium to peers (Reuters, cited in search results), and a US rally back into AI could pull the money out as fast as it came.
signals.for_you: Swing: INDA's break is confirmed by her rule (close over 52.13 on 1.5x volume). It is a dashboard buy point, not a setups.json swing: buy range up to 54.74, stop 50.90, about 3.8% under Friday's close. With the US in a correction, a small first piece only after the S&P 500 steadies, and no add if INDA closes back under 52.13. Puts: no INDA put idea (an ETF with no earnings, but not on the long term scan). Long term: no action.

signals.title: Medtronic Tuesday: what counts as a good quarter
signals.since_yesterday: New: the consensus numbers, the 6:45am ET release time, and TrendSpider added MDT to the long term scan this morning.
signals.what_happened: Medtronic reports fiscal Q2 2027 on Tuesday Nov 24, with the release at 5:45am CT (6:45am ET) and a webcast at 7:30am ET (Medtronic). Consensus is $1.34 a share on $9.47 billion of revenue, up 5.7% from a year ago; Earnings Whispers' own number is $1.37 (Finviz, Earnings Whispers preview). It is the first quarter without last year's extra week, so organic growth near 7% is the test. MDT closed 99.94 on Nov 20, just over its pullback zone (94.50 to 99.64), with the dashboard waiting for a close over 101.50; the long term point (94.50) is 5.8% under the price (dashboard).
signals.so_what: For a clinician the numbers to read are pulsed field ablation (Affera) growth in cardiac ablation, diabetes after the MiniMed separation, and any update on renal denervation coverage. Who gets paid if PFA keeps growing: MDT and Boston Scientific take share from older ablation tools. What would make this wrong: a guide cut blamed on hospital capital budgets, which would hit the whole medtech group.
signals.for_you: Swing: no MDT entry before the report. After it, the pullback setup needs a close over 101.50 on rising volume; its 6.1% stop is wider than the 6% swing limit, so it is a weak setup. Puts: no MDT puts across the report. Long term: MDT is over its zone; the TrendSpider long term scan added it, the dashboard says wait.

cycle.quadrant: Growth slowing while inflation stays high: late overheating, leaning toward stagflation
cycle.quadrant_why: No new data since Friday. Wednesday's PCE (core 3.2% a year expected) and Q3 GDP (3.5% expected) decide it (Yahoo Finance, Nov 22). The All Weather model is not changed.
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening and late, but the market has started to doubt the last hike: the two year yield fell the most since August 2025 on Friday, and the Treasury Secretary now argues against more tightening (Investing.com).
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. A Treasury Secretary pressing the Fed in public is a sign of how costly high rates are for a large federal debt.
cycle.big_cycle: Internal order and technology: the government is now probing the export compliance of the leader of the AI build out. External order: Asian governments are stepping in to support their markets (Taiwan buying, Korea readying a fund), and China's metals pause ends Nov 27.
tailwinds: Futures bounced and the two year yield fell, easing hike pressure.
Foreign money is moving into India rather than leaving emerging markets.
headwinds: Political pressure on the Fed and on Nvidia at the same time.
Korea's memory stocks kept falling with a rescue fund on standby.

history.what: Bespoke counts only five weeks with an S&P 500 loss every day and four drops of 1% or more, these two among them; both times stocks made lower lows months later (Yahoo Finance, Nov 21, 2026).
history.lesson: The first bounce after a violent week is rarely the low.

principle.text: Don't confuse what you wish were true with what is true (paraphrase of Principles).
principle.applied: After a week like last week, a green premarket screen feels like relief. What is true at 6am is a futures price. Judge it at the 4pm close, by the volume.
